title.narrative: Kenya Country Programme

description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Kenya Country Programme works to strengthen Kenya's role as the pre-eminent trade and transit hub for East Africa, building on over fifteen years of engagement since 2010 along the Northern Corridor and LAPSSET, which together serve as the primary trade gateway for Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, and eastern DRC. The Programme spans port and corridor infrastructure, including upgrades to the Port of Mombasa and One Stop Border Posts at Moyale, Malaba, Busia, and Taveta; digital trade systems such as the Kenya Revenue Authority Integrated Customs Management System and the Trade Logistics Information Pipeline (TLIP), and standards and export quality work spanning horticulture, tea, and food safety in support of Kenya's growing agri-export base. Under the current strategy, the Programme places added emphasis on green trade, including a flagship initiative to shift Kenya's horticultural exports from air to sea freight, alongside AfCFTA domestication, expansion of the iSOKO platform for small-scale traders, and climate-smart logistics and cool chain infrastructure to future-proof Kenya's trade.

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Quality/Value of traded goods in Kenya
Reduction in turnaround time of SQI services in KEBS conformity labs in Kenya

comment.narrative: 20 days initially
7% Reduction in turnaround time services for supported labs in Kenya - KEPHIS and KEBS
52% reduction in average testing turnaround time from 15 days to 7 after upgrades to Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) conformity laboratories that delivered faster and more reliable testing services.

title.narrative: Percentage reduction in turnaround time of standards and SPS services in KEPHIS conformity labs in Kenya

comment.narrative: 7% Reduction in turnaround time of standards and SPS services in KEPHIS conformity labs in Kenya

65% reduction in SPS testing services average turnaround time from 20 days to 7 following improvements of Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS) laboratories. They expanded their scope of test parameters, enabling a wider range of assessments to be completed efficiently.

title.narrative: Number of tests - SPS, food safety, and quality assessments conducted by KEBS

description.narrative: proficiency testing equipment having expanded KEBS scope of accreditation

comment.narrative: 25 additional tests can be conducted, from TMA's support towards proficiency testing equipment, having expanded KEBS scope of accreditation, from 201 to 226 tests. This has boosted the range of SPS, food safety, and quality assessments that KEBS can conduct, reducing reliance on external laboratories and facilitating faster compliance with international standards.

title.narrative: Improved physical interconnectivity and linkages in Kenya
Percentage of reduced trucks waiting time at port gates

description.narrative: Clearance time by improved Port Gates

comment.narrative: Smart gates installed at Gate 24 & 25 at Mombasa Port to reduce trucks waiting time at port gates 24 and 25 by 15%- base is 15 mins
Enhancing cargo throughput and reducing gate clearance time by 10% for improved Port Gates. Shipment of smart gates good and site installation competed in March 2026.

title.narrative: Reduce traffic congestion at Mombasa Port

description.narrative: Reduce traffic congestion at Mombasa Port by at least 5% after Installation of directional signage and yard marking for Phase 1 practically completed to

comment.narrative: Installation of directional signage and yard marking for Phase 1 practically completed to reduce traffic congestion at Mombasa Port by at least 5%
Phase 1 completedReduce traffic congestion at the port and improve port productivity and reduce dwell time by 2% in Mombasa Port

title.narrative: Increased Resilience and Empowerment of women, youth and other vulnerable traders in Kenya
Number of women owned SMEs participating in export market and increased income

description.narrative: Increase of women owned SMEs participating in export market and increased income

comment.narrative: 100 women SMEs trained on meeting international export standards and provided with market linkages to lead to a 10% increase of women owned SMEs participating in export market and increased income.--potentially trading 5000 USD

1269 women trained on complying with international market standards enhancing Trading capacity of women, youth, PWDs to Increase resilience and empowerment of women, youth and other vulnerable traders.

title.narrative: Greener goods and services
Kilowatts generated at the OSBPs through solarizations

description.narrative: Solarisation of Moyale and Malaba border posts generating 230KW of green energy to serve the border post including defects liability period. Solarasiation of LungaLunga OSBP to generate 250kw commenced.

comment.narrative: Solarisation of Moyale and Malaba border posts generating 230KW of green energy to serve the border post including defects liability period. Solarasiation of LungaLunga OSBP to generate 250kw commenced.

Increased resilience of trade-related infrastructure by use of solar from the current unreliable electricity from the grid Generate 450kW green energy to enhance cargo clearance and cross border trade .At the Malaba and Moyale One-Stop Border Posts, solarisation has been completed against a target of 230 kW of green energy capacity, delivering clean and reliable power to support border operations, including during the defects liability period.

title.narrative: Increased Market Access and Business Competitiveness
Value(USD) of investments leveraged from external sources to support TMA programs

comment.narrative: $1.4 million disbursed through the EASETRADE platform for supply-chain financing to about 40 SMEs in June 2026

title.narrative: Cumulative export value generated in USD(M)

comment.narrative: $12 million cumulative export value generated from 9,500 MT of fresh and value-added produce, linking 7,300 smallholder farmers to export markets

title.narrative: Number of jobs created, enhanced or sustained

comment.narrative: Cumulative 40,000 jobs sustained with interventions linked to Voluntary Sustainability Standards (VSS) uptake, operationalisation of the export supply hub (ESH), capacity building for farmer groups on GLOBAL G.A.P standards, structured market linkages between exporters, producers and certification of farmer groups

title.narrative: Efficient trade through innovative digital technologies
Percentage increase in transaction volume

comment.narrative: EWRS developed and deployed and is in use since Nov 2025.Endline to measure the results.Expected to increase by 10% utilisation eWRS and 10% increment in transaction volumes (issuance of Warehouse Receipts in eWRS and Fasttrack / increase export trade in progresss.
Actuals not realised yet and shall be updated upon data collection and validation

title.narrative: Percentage reduction in system downtime leading to reduced KRA clearance time

comment.narrative: 10% reduction in KRA clearance time

50% reduction in system downtime from the integrated customs management (iCMS)1platform from 128 hours in 2025 to 3 hours by March 2026 after system upgrade. The system achieved 99% record uptime post upgrade

Value of sales from TMA-supported market linkage initiatives

•$47,000 sales in food supplies and sweets to Zambia from TMA-supported market linkage initiatives with Kenya Association of Manufacturers.

comment.narrative: creation of packhouses and aggregation centres
5 packhouses/aggregation centres trading at least 5000

comment.narrative: targeted farmers under formal buyer contracts
50% of targeted farmers under formal buyer contracts.---with contract of atleast usd 5000 signed

3.4 MT shipment of apple mangoes exported to the UK as a promotional pilot to test market entry conditions, buyer interest, logistics and compliance, and to position Kenyan mangoes in the market. This was the first shipment of mangoes from Kenya to the UK since the Covid 19 period, restarting the exports in mangoes from Kenya to the UK
